answer: Every verifier locks a stake bond before countersigning transactions. Anyone submits proof of an invalid countersignature and the ledger burns that bond instantly, set above any epoch reward, so honest epochs can never repay one caught fraud. Sybil clones fail because each fake identity must post the same real bond: more clones mean more collateral exposed to slashing while returns dilute per clone. Trust settles slowly like shale, but slashing hits fast as wind shifts a dune, so agents verify honestly over a long horizon.
